- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.17) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.28) in recent days, model tends to underestimate prices; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 1–2 days); apply a 2–5 day lag correction: reduce forecast by 1–2% per day after spike.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of downward trend), model often fails to adjust; apply a 1–3 day mean-reversion bias correction: forecast = prior 3-day average + 0.5×(true - prior 3-day avg).  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window; apply a 1–2 day downward bias correction starting from day 5–7.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment spikes (e.g., -0.50, -0.28), model tends to overshoot downward; apply a 1–2 day upward bias correction after such events.
